chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, from Aban, from Abu al-Abbas al-Baqqaq, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Pre-emption is not valid except for a partner.'

key_terms.اَلشُّفْعَةُ: Pre-emption, the right of a co-owner or adjacent landowner to buy a shared property before it is sold to a third party.
key_terms.لِشَرِيكٍ: For a partner, referring to a co-owner in a shared asset.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of pre-emption (shuf'ah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the reliable chain of Aban ibn Taghlib, establishes a strict jurisprudential condition that the right of pre-emption (al-shuf'ah) is exclusive to co-owners (shuraka'), thereby preventing external parties from claiming priority in shared property sales. In Shia fiqh, this ruling underscores the principle of removing harm (darar) among partners by allowing them to maintain unity of ownership, a concept deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition and elaborated upon by scholars like Al-Tusi in his systematic compilation.
